periodos.nombre: Iron Age I — Conquered by Noba, territory of Manasseh

descripcion_geo: City in Gilead, in the territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Transjordan, conquered by a local leader called Noba, who gives it his own name after the victory, an example of post-conquest territorial renaming.
clima: Mountain Mediterranean in transition to semi-arid — dry and hot summers, cold winters, typical of the eastern Gilead region.
recursos: Position in the Manassite territory of Gilead
Agricultural and grazing lands in the region
importancia_estrategica: Kenat exemplifies a particular case within the Transjordan conquest system: unlike other generally tribally assigned cities, this one is specifically conquered by an individual named Noba, a descendant of Manasseh, who gives it his own name instead of maintaining the original Canaanite designation, showing individual agency within the collective process of tribal conquest.

otros_habitantes.descripcion: Original population of the city before its conquest by Noba, integrated into the Amorite-Gileadite territory of the region.
Family from the half-tribe of Manasseh who conquers and renames the city with their own name after the military victory.

historias.titulo: Noba conquers Kenat and gives it his name
historias.descripcion: Noba, belonging to the half-tribe of Manasseh, goes and takes Kenath and its villages, calling it Noba after his own name, in an individual act of conquest that replaces the original Canaanite appellation with that of the conqueror.

historias.titulo: Kenath in the chronicler genealogies of Manasseh
historias.descripcion: The genealogical lists of Chronicles confirm the possession of Kenath and its villages within the historical territory of Manasseh, recording its administrative persistence over several centuries.

historias.titulo: Kenath within the general territory of Gilead assigned to Manasseh
historias.descripcion: Kenat is part of the extensive territory of Gilead and Bashan corresponding to the half tribe of Manasseh in Transjordan, forming part of the set of cities conquered in this eastern region of Israelite territory.

personajes.descripcion: Member of the half-tribe of Manasseh who personally conquers Kenath and its villages, giving it his own name to replace the original Canaanite name.

personajes.nombre: Half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
personajes.rol: Holders of the territory that includes Kenat
personajes.descripcion: Tribe that receives the extensive territory of Gilead and Bashan, including Kenat among the cities individually conquered by its members.

personajes.rol: Inhabitants prior to the conquest of Noba
personajes.descripcion: Population displaced by the conquest of Noba, who replaced the original name of the city with his own after the victory.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Kenat lacks its own narrative or mythical development; Its value for the biblical corpus is to illustrate the pattern of individual conquest within the collective framework of tribal possession, where a specific member of Manasseh manages to rename conquered territory with his own name, a practice also documented in other similar cases from Transjordan that reflect the combination of individual initiative and collective tribal belonging in the general process of possession of the promised land.

mitos.nombre: The renaming of conquered cities as a practice of symbolic possession

judaismo.fuente_secundaria: Comentario rabínico tradicional sobre la práctica de renombrar ciudades conquistadas como Kenat (renombrada Noba) y otros casos similares en la Transjordania, como acto simbólico de posesión efectiva más allá de la mera asignación tribal formal
judaismo.descripcion: Jewish tradition observes that the practice of renaming individually conquered cities, as with Kenat-Noba, represents a symbolic act of effective possession that transcends mere theoretical tribal allocation, demonstrating that true appropriation of the promised land required concrete and committed action on the part of specific individuals and families within the broader collective framework of tribal heritage.
judaismo.significado_teologico: The renaming of conquered territories illustrates that the effective possession of the promised land combines the collective promise to the tribes with the concrete individual responsibility and action of its particular members.
